desc:
Rearrange the letters of s so that letters that occur more often come first. All copies of a letter must stay together in one block. If two letters occur equally often, the alphabetically smaller letter comes first, so the answer is unique. Return the rearranged string.

s = "tree"      result = "eert"
s = "cccaaa"    result = "aaaccc"
s = "abbcccd"   result = "cccbbad"
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Whatever order you choose, the letters of one kind must form one contiguous block, so you really only order the 26 kinds.
Count the occurrences of each letter, then order the letters by (count descending, letter ascending).
Build the answer by repeating each letter as many times as it occurred, in that order. Sorting 26 items is cheap; the string building dominates.
editorial: Count the letters (26 counters). The output is determined by the order of the kinds: sort the present letters by the key (-count, letter), then write each letter count times. Sorting the whole string character by character with a custom key gives the same result at O(n log n), but sorting only 26 kinds is O(n + 26 log 26).
If the alphabet were large, a bucket sort over counts (bucket k holds the letters occurring exactly k times) would keep the whole thing linear.
